topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecture and outlines its key learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents along with their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and pathway defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit specific cancer-cell vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, and impaired DNA repair machinery.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale, design, and clinical use of small-molecule kinase inhibitors as well as the diverse resistance mechanisms and off-target effects that arise.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches utilizing engineered antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against specific cell-surface proteins.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the basis of immune surveillance against tumors and various immunotherapy strategies that harness or engineer T cells to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Overall challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical survival trends, persistent systemic challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and emerging paradigms and dilemmas in the future of cancer care.
